artifact.self_contained_problem:
A graph is triangle-free if it contains no three mutually adjacent vertices. A graph is bipartite if its vertex set can be partitioned into two parts so that every edge has its endpoints in different parts. For a graph G, let b(G) denote the minimum number of edges whose deletion from G yields a bipartite graph.

Determine whether the following holds: for every real number ε > 0, there exists an integer n(ε) such that every triangle-free graph G on n > n(ε) vertices satisfies
   b(G) ≤ (1/25 + ε) n².
artifact.category_tag: Extremal graph theory (Erdős conjecture on triangle-free graphs)
artifact.status_search_result: The full conjecture (with constant 1/25) remains open. The current best known unconditional bound is approximately n²/23.5 (Balogh–Clemen–Lidický, 2021), improving the previous n²/18 bound. The conjecture has been verified for certain ranges of edge density (e.g., density ≤ 0.2486 or ≥ 0.3197), but the asymptotic statement with (1/25 + ε) for all sufficiently large n is not known.

status_evidence.title: Max Cuts in Triangle-free Graphs
status_evidence.snippet: every triangle-free graph can be made bipartite by removing at most n²/23.5 edges improving the previously best bound of n²/18
status_evidence.claim: Best unconditional upper bound is n²/23.5, still weaker than the conjectured n²/25.

status_evidence.title: Making a triangle-free graph bipartite (Erdős problems)
status_evidence.snippet: Erdős conjecture: every triangle-free graph on n vertices can be made bipartite by removing at most n²/25 edges
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture is listed as an open Erdős problem.
